A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Top-k Learning-to-Defer work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: V4 reports original classification and regression experiments in Section 6 and Appendix B, including accuracy, RMSE and consultation-budget results.

after.justification: V5 retains these original classification and regression results in Section 6 and Appendix B.

M1.justification: The Top-k selection procedure, k-independent surrogate, adaptive cardinality loss and Algorithms 1–2 are retained. New theoretical explanations do not specify a changed training or inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate one-stage L2D on CIFAR-10 and SVHN, and two-stage L2D on California Housing, SVHN and CIFAR-100, retaining the same expert-specialization scenarios.

E2.justification: Corresponding plots retain the same Top-1 L2D, random-allocation and, where plotted, oracle comparators. Newly cited related-work methods are not added as experimental baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix B retains the same splits, expert configurations, architectures, training budgets, consultation costs, regularization grid and evaluation metrics. No new evaluation protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: The existing budget/cardinality and aggregation-rule comparisons are retained. No ablation, robustness test, error analysis or case study is added; the new cardinality analysis is theoretical.

E5.justification: Both reproducibility statements specify four independent runs with fixed experts, fifty repetitions for random policies, and mean and standard deviation reporting with one-standard-deviation error bars.

E6.justification: The matched experimental tables and plots retain their numerical results and trends. V4 Tables 1–5 become v5 Tables 2–6; Figures 1 and 5–9 are retained, including the reported CIFAR-10 Top-k(x) majority-voting accuracy of 95.53%.

T1.justification: V5 adds a Bayes-optimal cardinality and marginal-risk derivation in Section 5 and Appendix A.12, explicitly asserts Hk-consistency for the adaptive surrogate, and formalizes stochastic experts in Section 3. It also replaces -U with +U minimizability-gap terms in v4 Theorems 3 and 12, now Theorems 3.3 and 4.7. These revise substantive guarantees, although several Appendix A.11 derivations retain the old signs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about unified Top-k deferral, adaptive Top-k(x), k-independent learning, consistency guarantees, cascade generalization and accuracy–cost advantages.

C2.justification: V5 gives a more explicit risk-based explanation of when additional expert consultation is justified, relating marginal predictive-error reduction to marginal cost. It also explicitly states that the theoretical framework accommodates stochastic experts.

D1.justification: The implementation information remains unchanged, including A100 hardware, model architectures, optimizers, hyperparameters, training algorithms and the statement that code, datasets and configurations are publicly released.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds references and brief discussion covering budgeted multiple-expert deferral, imbalanced deferral, online and expert-conditioned deferral, and additional surrogate analyses. The central research-gap and novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V5 adds appendix notation and definition subsections, a named Bayes-optimal cardinality discussion and an acknowledgment, alongside localized prose and terminology edits. Most existing narrative and the main section order remain intact.

P2.justification: The manuscript-wide switch to the ICLR template changes typography, author layout, running headers, spacing and figure/algorithm placement. V5 also adds notation Table 1 and renumbers the retained experimental tables; the experimental plots themselves are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The notation guide, stochastic-expert clarification and adaptive-risk derivation improve understanding of the existing framework. The corrected +U theorem statements improve precision, but Appendix A.11 still uses -U in Equations 21, 30 and 39, leaving the theoretical repair incomplete. The gains are therefore limited, with the methods and empirical evidence unchanged.
